content:
End of June was the target to have the Preventive Maintenance Push closed out. That came and went yesterday and it is still sitting open.

Brooke started this in early May, HVAC, plumbing and electrical across the whole portfolio, and I have been the QC eye on it. I logged both cluster spot-checks as passing in late May and my read is that my part of it is finished. The crew called the HVAC run wrapped around the same time.

Before I put my name to this closing out, I need to know where every piece of it stands as of today, cluster by cluster, and I need our records saying the same thing. Work out what is actually finished and what is not, and get our tracking to match. Anything still open gets its own tracking item raised, with the person who owns that work named on it. My own spot-check records are part of that, with a short note left on each one saying where it landed and why.

Anything flagged in the field that still needs a tech back onsite belongs in our maintenance ticket log rather than sitting as a tracking item, and put a slot on my calendar to go back out and re-inspect whatever ends up in that follow-up.

Then post where this stands in the channel the push has been running in so the crew is working off the same picture, and draft an email to Brooke, cluster by cluster, with what is open, who is holding it, and what has to happen before this can close.

I do not want Brooke's email written so it can be read either way. If my QC side is a pass, say pass. If it is not, say straight out that my earlier sign-off does not hold and this should not be treated as closeable yet, with the reasons.
I will investigate the status of the Preventive Maintenance Push across Linear, Slack, Airtable, Gmail
, and Google Calendar to determine the state of each cluster and spot-check record.

content: I will run a script to process
all downloaded Linear issues and list those relevant to the Preventive Maintenance Push across clusters.

parameters.description: Parse and display all PM Push related Linear issues.
parameters.command:
python3 -c "
import glob, json

files = glob.glob('/home/agent/.gemini/tmp/workspace/tool-outputs/session-c8d0cb03-0fd3-4fd5-811b-6f7b3ec97ecd/mcp_mcp429207a6_list_issues_*.txt')

all_issues = {}
for file in files:
    with open(file) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
        for issue in data.get('issues', []):
            all_issues[issue['identifier']] = issue

print(f'Total unique issues loaded: {len(all_issues)}')

pm_keywords = ['preventive', 'cluster', 'hvac', 'plumbing', 'electrical', 'spot', 'qc', 'south', 'north', 'east', 'west', 'central', 'coil', 'panel', 'water heater', 'hose bib']

pm_issues = []
for id_str in sorted(all_issues.keys(), key=lambda x: int(x.split('-')[1])):
    issue = all_issues[id_str]
    title = issue['title']
    desc = issue['description']
    proj = issue.get('project')
    proj_id = proj.get('id') if proj else None
    
    if proj_id == 'proj_003' or any(k in title.lower() or k in desc.lower() for k in pm_keywords):
        pm_issues.append(issue)

for issue in pm_issues:
    assignee = issue['assignee']['name'] if issue.get('assignee') else 'Unassigned'
    state = issue['state']['name']
    proj_id = issue.get('project', {}).get('id') if issue.get('project') else None
    print(f\"{issue['identifier']} | State: {state:12} | Assignee: {assignee:18} | Proj: {proj_id} | Title: {issue['title']}\")
"

parameters.description: Print all issues matching maintenance keywords.
parameters.command:
python3 -c "
import glob, json

files = glob.glob('/home/agent/.gemini/tmp/workspace/tool-outputs/session-c8d0cb03-0fd3-4fd5-811b-6f7b3ec97ecd/mcp_mcp429207a6_list_issues_*.txt')

all_issues = {}
for file in files:
    with open(file) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
        for issue in data.get('issues', []):
            all_issues[issue['identifier']] = issue

kw_list = ['south', 'north', 'east', 'west', 'plumbing', 'electrical', 'hvac', 'filter', 'spot', 'qc', 'panel', 'water heater', 'hose bib', 'push', 'preventive']

print(f'Total issues: {len(all_issues)}')
for id_str in sorted(all_issues.keys(), key=lambda x: int(x.split('-')[1])):
    issue = all_issues[id_str]
    title = issue['title']
    desc = issue['description']
    text = (title + ' ' + desc).lower()
    if any(k in text for k in kw_list):
        assignee = issue['assignee']['name'] if issue.get('assignee') else 'Unassigned'
        proj = issue.get('project', {}).get('id') if issue.get('project') else None
        print(f\"{issue['identifier']} | {issue['state']['name']:12} | Assignee: {assignee:18} | Proj: {str(proj):10} | Title: {title}\")
"

import glob, json

        data = json.load(f)

target_ids = ['OPS-16', 'OPS-17', 'OPS-18', 'OPS-28', 'OPS-35', 'OPS-40', 'OPS-43', 'OPS-44', 'OPS-51', 'OPS-56', 'OPS-66', 'OPS-71', 'OPS-79', 'OPS-81', 'OPS-87', 'OPS-91', 'OPS-96', 'OPS-97', 'OPS-98', 'OPS-99', 'OPS-108', 'OPS-186']

**Preventive Maintenance Push - Portfolio Closeout Audit & Current Status Update (July 1, 2026)**

parameters.body:
Hi Brooke,

Following the end-of-June target date for closing out the portfolio-wide Preventive Maintenance Push, I performed a full cluster-by-cluster audit today (July 1, 2026) across our Linear tracking, Airtable maintenance logs, and field reports to determine whether the initiative is ready to be closed.

To be direct: from the Quality Control perspective, this initiative is NOT A PASS for full closeout. My earlier partial QC sign-offs logged in late May (covering the initial South, North, and East HVAC runs) do NOT hold as a portfolio-wide sign-off, and this push should NOT be treated as closeable yet.

Here is the exact status and open items cluster by cluster, who is holding each piece, and what must occur before we can close:

1. SOUTH CLUSTER
- Status: OPEN (Field Work Pending)
- Completed Work: HVAC coil cleaning/filter swaps (Elias Navarro) passed QC spot-checks. Electrical panel inspections (Patricia Nguyen) are complete (OPS-186 updated to Done). Initial plumbing inspection was completed by Carlos Mendez.
- What is Open: Carlos Mendez's plumbing inspection flagged field repairs requiring techs back onsite: replacing two water heaters past serviceable life and repairing multiple leaking/damaged hose bibs.
- Who is Holding It: Carlos Mendez (Field Maintenance Lead).
- Action Required: These field repairs have been transferred out of tracking into Airtable maintenance tickets MT-2026-1327 (water heater replacements) and MT-2026-1328 (hose bib repairs). Carlos's team must complete the physical repairs, after which I will conduct an onsite re-inspection (slot hold on my calendar for July 8).

2. NORTH CLUSTER
- Status: CLOSED / PASS
- Completed Work: HVAC coil cleaning, filter replacements, electrical panel checks, and plumbing audits are 100% complete (Tony Reyes / Wesley Tran).
- QC Verification: Passed QC spot-checks on May 25 (OPS-87, OPS-98). All tracking records (OPS-40, OPS-44) are aligned and marked Done.

3. EAST CLUSTER
- Status: CLOSED / PASS
- Completed Work: HVAC coil service and general PM inspections complete (Elias Navarro).
- QC Verification: Passed QC spot-check in late May (OPS-99). Tracking records updated to Done.

4. WEST CLUSTER
- Status: OPEN (Execution & QC Outstanding)
- Completed Work: Condenser coil cleaning and filter swaps complete (OPS-91, Lisa Smith / John Smith).
- What is Open: Full PM execution and property wrap-up remain in progress under OPS-35. Furthermore, because field execution was not wrapped up, I have NOT performed a QC spot-check for the West Cluster.
- Who is Holding It: Brooke Phillips (Project Lead) & Lisa Smith / John Smith (Field Execution Leads) for PM wrap-up; Jaime Salinas (QC Inspector) for the pending QC spot-check.
- Action Required: Lisa and John must finalize remaining PM field work and confirm completion on OPS-35. Once field work is confirmed complete, I will conduct the West Cluster QC spot-check (tracked under newly raised item OPS-1000).

SUMMARY OF WHAT HAS TO HAPPEN BEFORE CLOSEOUT:
1. South Cluster: Carlos Mendez completes plumbing field repairs (MT-2026-1327 and MT-2026-1328); Jaime Salinas re-inspects and clears the work.
2. West Cluster: Lisa Smith and John Smith complete field execution (OPS-35); Jaime Salinas conducts and passes the West Cluster QC spot-check (OPS-1000).

Until all field work in the South Cluster clears QC re-inspection and the West Cluster is fully executed and passed on QC inspection, the Preventive Maintenance Push must remain open.

Best regards,

Jaime Salinas
Quality Control Inspector
Star Property Management
